lines.text: You have one small task. It takes ten minutes.
Three hours later, you've cleaned your room, watched six videos, and learned how penguins sleep.
Here's what most people get wrong.
When a task makes you feel bored, anxious, or not good enough, your brain treats that feeling like a threat.
So it reaches for something that feels better right now. Your phone. A snack. Anything else.
Researchers call this short term mood repair. You buy relief today, and pay for it with stress tomorrow.
And every time you dodge the task, it feels a little scarier the next time.
So how do you break the cycle?
One. Shrink the task until it feels silly. Don't write the essay. Just open the document.
Two. Set a timer for five minutes. Your brain can handle almost anything for five minutes.
Three. Forgive yourself for last time. In one study, students who forgave themselves procrastinated less before the next exam.
So. What are you avoiding right now?
